livelihood_summary: Highly productive surplus rain-fed farming with some livestock, fishing, hunting and forest products; good cross-border markets
main_crops: Maize, sorghum, groundnuts, soya, cassava, sweet potatoes, rice, vegetables; Robusta coffee as cash crop
seasonal_calendar: Two rainy seasons (Mar-Jun, Aug-Nov); land preparation Jan-Mar; planting mid-Mar to May; cereal harvest Jul-Aug and Nov-Dec
main_hazards: Dry spells May-Jul (about every 2 years); river and stream floods Aug-Oct (about every 4 years); crop pests every rainy season; conflict and insecurity
coping_and_notes: Wild foods, bush product and charcoal sales, labor migration, remittances, livestock sales
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, p.10-13
lean_season: Dry-season stocks decline from about Apr; lean season ends late Jun when green maize is eaten
flood_pattern: River and stream floods Aug-Oct, about every 4 years; seasonal flooding makes some roads impassable in the rains
wealth_determinants: Land cultivated (poor about 0.8 ha, hand tools; better-off 2-4 ha with hired labor and tractors), crop types grown in both seasons, productive assets
markets_and_trade: Border markets Nabiapai and Bazi (DRC, Kenya, Uganda); Yambio, Yei, Ikotos, Nimule, Namaku, Koliko; surplus maize sold to traders and WFP (P4P); roads to Juba; several currencies in use
consumption_calendar_poor: Own crops normally last poor households about 9 months (Jul-Mar), now 4-7 months; market purchase of maize, sorghum and other foods for remaining months; wild food consumption peaks in rains; better-off largely self-sufficient
income_and_expenditure: Poor: bush product sales, labor, brewing; better-off: food and cash crop (coffee) sales, retail trade; livestock sales peak in dry season
access_constraints: Poor road maintenance and seasonal flooding make some roads impassable in the rains; insecurity; long distances; inflation; displacement to Uganda and IDP camps

livelihood_summary: Moderately productive agro-pastoral zone: cereals and legumes, cattle and small livestock
main_crops: Sorghum (main), millet, maize, groundnut, sesame, cassava, sweet potatoes, vegetables
seasonal_calendar: Single rainy season Apr-early Nov; land preparation Feb-Mar; planting Apr-May; weeding Jun-Jul; lean season Jun-Jul; groundnut and sesame harvest from Aug, sorghum from Oct
main_hazards: Drought about every 12 years; annual crop pests and livestock disease; periodic river floods; inter-clan conflict
coping_and_notes: Poor sell firewood, charcoal, grass, mats, shea oil, wild foods and labor; better-off sell sorghum, millet, cattle and honey
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, p.14-17
wealth_determinants: Land size cultivated (poor 0.42-0.84 ha, fewer than 5 goats or sheep; better-off over 20 goats/sheep and cattle, ox-plows, tractors, power saws)
markets_and_trade: Rumbek, Yirol, Terekeka, Cueibet, Wulu, Mvolo, Tonj, Wau, Juba; corridors Juba-Rumbek-Wau and Maridi-Mvolo-Rumbek; goods mostly from Juba and Uganda
consumption_calendar_poor: Own cereal normally lasts 8 months (Aug-Mar), now 3-5 months; poor buy sorghum Apr-Jul and millet Jun-Jul; cassava year-round
income_and_expenditure: Lean-season income from firewood, charcoal, thatching grass; better-off sell sorghum, millet, vegetables, cattle, honey; health expenses peak Jun-Aug
access_constraints: Unpaved roads hard to use in the rains; very high inflation (up to 10-20 times for some goods since 2016); interclan conflict; tsetse and cattle disease

livelihood_summary: Cereal-deficit agricultural zone with minor livestock; single growing season; access to wild foods and gold extraction
main_crops: Maize, sorghum, millet, groundnuts, cowpeas, sweet potatoes, vegetables
seasonal_calendar: Rainy season Apr-Nov; dry planting from March; weeding Apr-Jun; harvest from Aug; dry spells Jun-Jul; lean season Jun-Aug
main_hazards: Floods at least once every 2 years in the rainy season (Apr-Nov); mid-season dry spells May-Jun; annual crop pests; conflict
coping_and_notes: Sale of charcoal, bamboo, wild game, honey, gold and agricultural labor
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, p.18-21
flood_pattern: Floods at least every 2 years in the rainy season (Apr-Nov); lowland market access affected
wealth_determinants: Land cultivated and livestock, especially cattle (poor under 1 ha and no livestock except chickens; better-off at least 5 cattle, ox-plows or tractors, 1.4-2 ha)
markets_and_trade: Juba, Torit, Lafon and Kapoeta trading centers; Nimule and Tseretenya border points with Uganda; routes Juba-Torit, Juba-Nimule, Torit-Ikotos; barter (for example tobacco) common
consumption_calendar_poor: Poor rely on own crops about 7 months, now 3-4 months; buy sorghum and maize Mar/Apr to Aug; wild foods available up to 6 months
income_and_expenditure: Poor: labor, charcoal, bamboo, gold extraction; better-off: crop sales, petty trade, timber; school fees Mar-Apr
access_constraints: Poor roads, insecurity, long distances, flooding of lowlands in the rains; staple prices up 7-8 times in Torit and Juba since 2016 while wages rose 2-3 times

zone_name: Western plains groundnuts, sesame and sorghum
livelihood_summary: Subsistence rain-fed farming with forest products, seasonal fishing and small livestock; formerly a surplus area
main_crops: Groundnuts and sesame (cash), sorghum, maize, cassava, cowpeas, pumpkins, vegetables
seasonal_calendar: Rainy season Apr-Oct; land preparation Feb-Apr; planting May to mid-Jun; weeding mid-Jun to Jul; green harvest from Sep; sorghum and sesame harvested in March
main_hazards: Dry spells and late season start about every 2 years (May-Jun); crop pests Jun-Dec; livestock disease; cross-border conflict; price spikes
coping_and_notes: Groundnut sales; natural product sales (charcoal, grass, bamboo, honey, shea); sorghum in-kind labor
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, p.22-24
lean_season: Not stated; green harvest from Sep, sorghum and sesame harvested in Mar
flood_pattern: Seasonal flooding limits market access; floods along rivers and low-lying areas are periodic
wealth_determinants: Land size, farming tools and labor (poor hand tools, short of labor; better-off ox-plows, bicycles, timber and bamboo)
markets_and_trade: Raja, Aroyo, Kuarjena, Mapel, Kangi, Bar Mayen, Aweil, Namatina, Duma, Nagero; Wau; South Darfur (Sudan)
consumption_calendar_poor: Own cereal normally 9 months (Sep-May), now 4-6 months; poor buy sorghum Jun-Aug with few income sources in those months; cassava year-round and in-kind labor cushion shortfalls
income_and_expenditure: Poor: groundnut sales, natural products (charcoal, bamboo, honey, shea); better-off: groundnut, sesame, cassava, sorghum, tobacco, timber; school fees Mar-Apr
access_constraints: Seasonal flooding and poor roads; LRA insecurity in neighboring CAR; staple prices up 6-10 times at Wau market since 2016 while labor wages rose 2 times

livelihood_summary: Pastoral with very limited cropping; milk, meat, blood and wild foods; food mainly bought or exchanged for livestock
main_crops: Sorghum (small amounts, mostly bought); milk and blood
seasonal_calendar: Rainy season Jun-Oct; seasonal livestock migration to grazing and water; livestock-for-grain trade
main_hazards: Inter-communal conflict and cattle raiding (dry season Nov-Feb); flooding Jul-Oct; livestock disease; drought
coping_and_notes: Livestock sales, herding and domestic labor, gold mining, charcoal and wild foods
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, p.25-27
lean_season: Mar-Jul (peak); purchase of sorghum most of the year
wealth_determinants: Number and type of livestock per household (small herds and few goats for poor; large herds, goats, camels and donkeys for better-off)
markets_and_trade: Nadapal, Kapoeta, Pibor; Torit, Juba, Lokichoggio (Kenya), Nakua (Ethiopia); livestock bartered for grain with Murle cultivators in SS03
consumption_calendar_poor: Poor cover only about 2 months of staple needs from own crops; buy sorghum most of the year except Aug-Sep; milk, meat and blood from herds, mostly via herding labor
income_and_expenditure: Livestock sales most critical; poor: herding labor, charcoal, firewood, wild foods (charcoal main income Jan-Apr); better-off: milk and milk products, gold
access_constraints: Poor roads, cattle raiding, insecurity, unreliable markets; livestock prices fall in drought; livestock leave the zone Nov-Dec and return Apr-May

livelihood_summary: Agro-pastoral: rain-fed cultivation and cattle, with fishing, hunting and wild foods; known cereal deficit area
seasonal_calendar: Rainy season Mar-Oct; land preparation Jan-Feb; planting Apr-Jun; weeding Jun-Aug; harvest Aug-Nov; lean season May-Jul; livestock migration Dec-Apr
main_hazards: Flooding every year Jul-Oct; livestock disease May-Nov; crop pests Jun-Sep; drought once in three years; cattle raiding Feb-May
coping_and_notes: Own cereal now lasts 2-4 months instead of 9; poor households sell charcoal, firewood, goats and labor; Sobat and Nile are central to livestock movement
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, p.28-30
wealth_determinants: Number and type of livestock, area cultivated per household, and productive assets such as canoes and fishing equipment (poor: few goats, small plots, hand tools; better-off: cattle and more land)
markets_and_trade: Local: Bor Marol, Panyagor, Akobo, Langkien; external: border markets in Uganda and Kenya; local markets supplied from Malakal; Akobo has seasonal trade with Ethiopia via Sobat/Pibor; Bor market links to Juba
consumption_calendar_poor: Sorghum harvest normally lasts 9 months (Aug-Apr), now 2-4 months; market purchases of sorghum peak in the lean period; poor sell livestock in the lean season, better-off Nov-May
income_and_expenditure: Poor: firewood, charcoal, poles, goats, home brew, agricultural labor; better-off: surplus crops, cattle, milk; livestock drug and health spending peaks in the rains
access_constraints: Rural roads lacking and rainy-season access depends on road condition; periodic conflict; Jonglei canal (dysfunctional) restricts livestock movement; Bor prices up significantly since 2016

zone_name: Northwestern flood plain sorghum and cattle
livelihood_summary: Classic agro-pastoral flood-plain system; cereal deficit imported from Sudan; cattle sold to Sudan; fishing and wild foods
main_crops: Sorghum (staple), maize, pearl millet, legumes, sesame, groundnuts
seasonal_calendar: Rainy season May-Oct; dry period peaks Jan-Apr; land preparation Mar-Apr; planting May-Jul; green harvest Aug-Sep; main harvest Oct-Nov
main_hazards: Rainfall variability; flash floods in low-lying areas Jul-Aug; striga and fall armyworm; livestock disease; conflict
coping_and_notes: Sale of labor, fish, wild foods and small livestock; better-off sell livestock and crops
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, p.31-34
flood_pattern: Flash floods in low-lying areas Jul-Aug
wealth_determinants: Household labor and ability to hire labor decide land size (poor up to 0.5 ha with hand tools and labor sold to better-off; better-off 2 ha or more); about 80% of households own cattle
markets_and_trade: Border markets Amiet, Majok, Chanwandit; Kuajok, Gogrial, Wunrok, Turalei, Aweil, Warawar, Nyamlel and others; sorghum imported from Sudan, cattle and gum arabic exported
consumption_calendar_poor: Poor harvest normally lasts about 6 months (Oct/Nov-Mar/Apr), now 2-5 months or 3 months; Mar-Apr combines purchased sorghum and sorghum earned through labor; wild foods peak in the rains
income_and_expenditure: Labor sales (peak Apr-May), fish, wild foods, small livestock; better-off sell livestock and crops; livestock sales peak Jun-Jul; seasonal labor migration Jan-Jun to Sudan, Amiet, Wau, Juba
access_constraints: Roads fully accessible in dry season, only partly in the rains; sorghum price up nearly 5 times since 2016; cattle raiding Feb-May; conflict and displacement in the south-east of the zone

livelihood_summary: Fishing, rain-fed cropping, livestock and wild foods on a narrow swampy floodplain along the Nile; river ports critical for trade
main_crops: Sorghum (staple), maize, cowpeas, groundnuts, vegetables (okra, pumpkins)
seasonal_calendar: Fishing year-round, lowest in the rains; land preparation Feb-Mar; harvest Sep-Nov; vegetables in dry season; livestock sales Feb-Jul; fish sales Jan-Apr and Aug-Nov
main_hazards: Flooding every 3-5 years plus the annual river rise; crop pests; livestock disease; localized cattle raiding
coping_and_notes: Sorghum harvest normally lasts 6-7 months, now 2-4; poor households sell fish, firewood, papyrus mats and brew
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, p.35-37
lean_season: Poor households buy sorghum from about Mar after own stocks run out; fish sales Jan-Apr and Aug-Nov
flood_pattern: Flooding every 3-5 years plus the annual river rise
wealth_determinants: Land cultivated (poor about 0.5 ha; better-off over 1 ha), fishing equipment and livestock
markets_and_trade: Malakal (main fish market, outside zone), Gut Thom (livestock, cereals, fish), Panyijiar, Awerial, Ayod (livestock); five river ports (Malakal, Adok, Shambe, Bor, Juba) critical for trade
consumption_calendar_poor: Poor sorghum harvest normally 6-7 months (mid-Aug to Feb), now 2-4 months; buy sorghum from March and maize from January; fish sales Jan-Apr and Aug-Nov
income_and_expenditure: Poor: fish, river products, wild foods, firewood, papyrus mats, brew, labor; better-off: milk, fish, crops, livestock, retail trade; school fees paid Apr, Jul, Oct
access_constraints: Wetland logistics: roads beyond the river difficult and seasonally unreliable; transport by canoe and motor boat; displacement and conflict disrupt fishing and farming; Bor sorghum and maize prices up 5-7 times since 2016

zone_name: North-western Nile basin cattle and maize
livelihood_summary: Livestock-focused agro-pastoral; maize is main staple; fishing and wild foods; deficit cereal producer relying on trade
seasonal_calendar: Rainy season May-Nov; dry spell May-Jun; floods Jul-Aug; livestock disease peaks Feb-Apr; fishing mostly in dry season
main_hazards: Floods Jul-Aug; dry spell May-Jun; bird plagues; striga and fall armyworm; dry-season cattle raiding
coping_and_notes: Poor households may buy up to 9 months of staples instead of 2-3; sell goats, sheep, labor and bush products
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, p.38-40
wealth_determinants: Livestock and land (poor few goats and under 1 ha; better-off cattle and over 1 ha, fishing equipment)
markets_and_trade: Rubkona (Bentiu) primary market; Mayom; routes west via Mayom-Abiemnhom, north via Pariang to South Kordofan, south by river via Adok-Panyijiar-Juba; trade with Sudan
consumption_calendar_poor: Poor maize harvest normally lasts mid-Aug to Feb (6-7 months), now purchase up to 9 months of staple needs; market purchases from March; lean months Jun-Jul
income_and_expenditure: Lean-season income from firewood, elephant grass and domestic work; better-off sell cattle, small livestock, surplus maize, timber; three school fee payments a year
access_constraints: Inter- and intra-communal attacks and cattle rustling in the dry season; Bentiu prices up 10 times for maize and 3 times for sorghum since 2016

livelihood_summary: Sobat River flood plain: maize, cattle and fishing; predictable annual inundation; net cereal importer; isolated, few trading opportunities
main_crops: Maize (main, two seasons), sorghum, cowpeas, vegetables
seasonal_calendar: Rainy season May-Oct (maize planted May); flood-recession maize from Nov, harvested late Feb-Mar; dry period most critical Jan-Apr; milk peaks Jul-Oct; peak goat and cattle sales Jun-Jul
main_hazards: Rainfall interruption in Jun-Jul; sudden swing to heavy rain early in the season; annual swamp inundation Aug-Sep (expected, not classed as flood); crop pests; livestock disease
coping_and_notes: Labor migration, sale of natural products, dried fish, goats and cattle
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, p.41-43
lean_season: Starts after Mar-Apr (wild food purchases before lean season)
flood_pattern: Annual Sobat inundation Aug-Sep is expected (not classed as flood); flood-recession maize from Nov
wealth_determinants: Land cultivated (poor 0.25-0.5 ha; better-off 1 ha or more) and cattle
markets_and_trade: Jikmir, Jekow and Mathiang main markets; goods moved by boat or head-load to local markets; imports sorghum, salt, soap, beer; exports cattle, goats, fish, bush products
consumption_calendar_poor: Poor maize harvest normally lasts about 6.5 months (mid-Aug to Feb), now about 2 months; own vegetables Mar-Aug; buy maize and vegetables the rest of the year; lean months May-Jul; wild foods Dec-Apr
income_and_expenditure: Firewood and domestic work year-round; elephant grass sold at high-expenditure periods; fishing prominent Oct-Dec, limited May-Aug; honey Dec-Mar; school fees three payments a year
access_constraints: Poor market access from insecurity, poor infrastructure and geographic isolation; conflict reduced cultivation, disrupted pasture, caused displacement and border closure

livelihood_summary: Semi-arid agro-pastoral with riverine area along the Nile; mechanized farming near the river; overall cereal deficit
seasonal_calendar: Single rainy season May-Oct; land preparation late Mar-early May; planting May-Jun; sorghum harvest Oct-Nov; own crops exhausted May-Aug; cattle sales May-Aug; milk peak to December
main_hazards: Floods every 2-3 years Aug-Oct; delayed or interrupted rains every 3-5 years around Jun-Jul; sorghum rust, grasshoppers, birds; livestock disease
coping_and_notes: Local and seasonal labor, livestock and crop sales, fish, wild foods, retail trade
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, p.44-46
wealth_determinants: Land (poor 0.5 ha; better-off 1-2 ha), livestock including cattle; mechanized and irrigated farming near the Nile
markets_and_trade: Malakal key market; strong two-way trade with Sudan (cereal in; cattle, goats, sheep, dried fish and bush products out); transport by river and road; rainy-season transport very limited
consumption_calendar_poor: Poor sorghum harvest used to last 6-7 months, now 2-4 months; food earned for labor, and market purchase when stocks run out; agricultural labor available Apr-Dec
income_and_expenditure: Sale of labor to better-off, seasonal labor migration, small livestock, fresh and dried fish, wild foods, firewood, beer; about two-thirds of labor is local
access_constraints: 2015 border closures caused severe price rises (sorghum up to 6 times since 2016); conflict hit mechanized farms (Renk, Manyo, Melut); banditry; annual Falata herds migrate into parts of the zone

zone_name: Maize, sorghum, fish and natural resources
livelihood_summary: South-eastern Jonglei highlands and lowlands bordering Ethiopia: agriculture with livestock, fishing and natural resources
main_crops: Maize, sorghum, groundnuts, cassava (bridges shortfalls Jan-Jul)
seasonal_calendar: Rainy season Mar-Dec; land preparation Feb; planting Mar; weeding Apr; first harvest Jul-Aug; second season from Sep, harvest from Dec; short dry season Jan-Feb
main_hazards: Floods every year in the wet season; livestock disease in the dry season; dry spells every 2-3 years; cattle rustling in the dry season; human disease peaks in the wet season
coping_and_notes: Labor, natural products (grass, firewood, charcoal), goat and sheep sales, wild foods and fish
source: FEWS NET South Sudan Livelihood Zone Map and Descriptions, Aug 2018, p.47-50
flood_pattern: Floods every year in the wet season
wealth_determinants: Land cultivated and livestock (poor goats and sheep, hand tools; better-off cattle, bicycles, motorcycles and vehicles, animal traction and hired labor)
markets_and_trade: Pochalla, Boma and Pibor; Punyido and Dima in Ethiopia; cross-border trade with Ethiopia and supplies from Kenya via Narus
consumption_calendar_poor: Poor buy sorghum Mar-Jun; cassava consumed mainly Jan-Jul to bridge shortfalls; green consumption from May; lean season Mar-Jul
income_and_expenditure: Poor: labor, natural products (grass, firewood, charcoal), goats and sheep, wild foods and fish; better-off: maize, sorghum, millet, timber, fish, petty trade; school fees Mar-Apr
access_constraints: Hilly terrain and poor roads; markets reachable in the short dry season (Jan-Feb) but access worsens in the rains; seasonal migration for labor to Kapoeta, Juba, Gambella, Dima
